<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from catalog/. Do not edit. -->

| Term | Also called | Meaning | See also |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Alpha** | Transparency | The fourth channel of a pixel. 255 means fully opaque and 0 means fully transparent. |  |
| **Alpha weighting** | Premultiplied alpha | Averaging colors weighted by their alpha, so that transparent pixels add no color. It avoids dark fringes around transparent areas. | Alpha |
| **Anchor** |  | The kernel cell that sits on top of the pixel being computed. It is usually the center. | Kernel |
| **Border mode** |  | The rule for inventing pixel values outside the image edge, so that windows near the edge still have values. |  |
| **Channel scope** | Channels | Which part of a color image a filter changes. RGB changes every channel. Brightness only changes luma and keeps the color differences. Color only does the opposite. | Luma |
| **Convolution** |  | The same as correlation, but with the kernel flipped in both directions first. For symmetric kernels the two give the same result. | Correlation |
| **Correlation** |  | Sliding a kernel over the image and summing weight times pixel at each position. PixelNexus applies kernels this way, like OpenCV. | Convolution |
| **Feathering** |  | Softening the edge of a selection so that the filtered area fades into the rest of the image. |  |
| **Gamma** |  | The exponent of a power curve that maps pixel values to output values. Below 1 it brightens the midtones, above 1 it darkens them. |  |
| **Gaussian noise** |  | Noise where each pixel gets a random amount added, drawn from a normal distribution with mean 0. | Sigma |
| **Gradient** |  | How fast brightness changes at a pixel, and in which direction. It has a horizontal part Gx and a vertical part Gy. |  |
| **Impulse noise** | Salt-and-pepper noise | Noise that replaces some pixels with extreme values, often pure white or black, instead of adding a small amount to all of them. | Median |
| **Kernel** | Mask, Filter mask | A small grid of weights. The filter multiplies each weight by the pixel under it and adds the results. | Convolution, Correlation |
| **Laplacian** |  | The sum of the second derivatives along x and y. It is 0 on flat areas and on straight ramps, and large at fine detail and edges. | Gradient |
| **Linear light** |  | Pixel values decoded from sRGB, so that the numbers are proportional to light intensity. Blurs in linear light behave more like real optics. | Luminance, Gamma |
| **Luma** |  | A brightness value made from gamma-encoded red, green and blue values with fixed weights. |  |
| **Luminance** |  | Brightness computed from linear light values with fixed weights for red, green and blue. Luma is the same sum on gamma-encoded values. | Luma, Linear light |
| **Mask** | Selection mask | An image of the same size where each value from 0 to 255 says how much of the filter result to use at that pixel. |  |
| **Median** |  | The middle value after sorting. Half of the values are at or below it, half at or above it. | Order statistic |
| **Neighborhood** | Window | The group of pixels around the current pixel that a filter looks at. |  |
| **Normalized kernel** |  | A kernel whose weights add up to 1. It keeps flat areas at the same brightness. | Kernel |
| **Order statistic** | Rank | A value picked by its position in the sorted list of window values, such as the minimum, the median or the maximum. | Median |
| **Output mapping** |  | The rule that turns signed results, such as gradients, into 8-bit values from 0 to 255. The computed values do not change, only how they are shown. |  |
| **Point operation** |  | A filter where each output pixel depends only on the same input pixel, such as gamma correction. It needs no neighbors. |  |
| **Point spread function** | PSF | The pattern that a single bright point becomes after blurring. It describes the blur completely for linear blurs. |  |
| **Seed** |  | The starting number of a random generator. The same seed always gives the same random numbers, so results can be repeated. |  |
| **Separable kernel** | Separable filter | A 2D kernel that equals one 1D kernel along the rows times one along the columns. The filter can then run as two fast 1D passes. | Kernel |
| **Sigma** | Standard deviation | The spread of a Gaussian curve, in pixels. A larger sigma means a wider, smoother blur. |  |
| **Spectrum** | Fourier spectrum | A picture of how much of each spatial frequency the image contains. The center holds slow changes and the edges hold fast changes. |  |
| **Support radius** | Halo | How far from a pixel a filter reads. A region is padded by this many pixels on every side, so its result matches a run on the whole image. | Neighborhood, Border mode |
